q6.answer: Order is the coordinator that moves each checkout to the next step. The record of progress is Order's own status on the order row (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, cancelled states), with status history. Changes are compare-and-set and written with outbox rows. For a claim in flight, payment_succeeded_at and claim_started_at are also stored there.

q7.answer: The provider sends a webhook to Payment's endpoint, which verifies the signature. Payment records the outcome in one transaction with an outbox row, and the relay publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. Order consumes that event and finishes the order.

q8.answer: There are two layers. Payment inserts the provider event id into processed_webhooks in the same transaction as the payment update, so a repeat hits the unique key, is ignored, and gets a 200. Downstream, Order acts on its current status, so a repeated PaymentSucceeded on a CONFIRMED order is ignored. Claim and refund also use idempotency keys.

q9.answer: On PaymentDeclined, Order marks the order CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled. That event triggers Inventory's release. If the reservation is HELD, it becomes RELEASED and the stock goes back on sale. If it is EXPIRED, it becomes RELEASED with no stock change because the stock is already back on sale. RELEASED or CLAIMED is ignored.

q10.answer: On PaymentSucceeded with the order AWAITING_PAYMENT, Order asks Inventory to claim. Inventory locks the reservation row. If it is still HELD, it becomes CLAIMED, even past 10 minutes. If it is EXPIRED, Inventory tries to retake every line in one transaction. If all are in stock, it claims and the order is CONFIRMED. If any line is short, it takes nothing, sets RELEASED and refuses, so the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with REFUND_PENDING and a full refund.

q11.answer: Payment owns refund execution. A failed or timed-out refund is marked FAILED_RETRYING, attempts increase, and next_attempt_at is set with growing backoff. A retry worker keeps retrying with the same key (refund: + order id). At the attempt limit it alerts ops once and keeps retrying at a slow interval, and ops can force a retry now. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table, unique on order id. Order's refund_status (REFUND_PENDING, then REFUNDED) only records that a refund was requested and whether it finished. The refund attempt limit, backoff and slow interval have no value yet.

q12.answer: Order's OrderConfirmed event, which carries the snapshot's lines, causes it, and Cart does the clearing. Cart removes each snapshot line or reduces its quantity, removing it at zero. Items added during the payment window stay. Cart records the order id in processed_events so a repeat does nothing.
